thread.title: Intraday Update: A Remixed Dow Goes Into Damage Control

author: Crystal Kim
title: Intraday Update: A Remixed Dow Goes Into Damage Control
text:
By Crystal Kim June 26, 2018 1:25 p.m. ET Stocks are back in the saddle Tuesday after a harrowing start to the week in which the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell more than 2% at its low. In today's Intraday Update , we...
•...assess the damage in the Dow and the S&P 500 ;
•...say goodbye to General Electric (GE) and hello to Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA);
•...explain why Avis Budget (CAR) and Hertz Global Holdings (HTZ) are sliding.
What's the Damage? After a severe pullback, the Dow has risen more than 70 points, or 0.3%, to 24,327.32. Meanwhile the S&P 500 has gained 0.2% to 2728 and the Nasdaq Composite has climbed 0.4% to 7562.91.
Big picture: Investors are going to be watching the S&P 500 for a comeback and it has to be a big enough to recover from the index's worst decline in two months. As Instinet technical analyst Frank Cappelleri outlined in his morning note: "One bullish pattern is now history. Another remains alive. The third is still under construction. However, a dead-cat bounce could produce our first bearish pattern in quite some time."
 The good news is that the most recent pullback is fairly small relative to the February dip and the one in April, and subsequent corrections have gradually notched higher lows. If the S&P 500 gaps up to a new high, it has a chance. If it struggles, beware of the dead cat, also known as the bear in bull's clothing.
One strategist maintained his view that all selloffs are opportunities to buy. Contrary to yesterday's analysis— that trade wars were weighing on stocks— Tigress Financial Intelligence's chief market strategist Ivan Feinseth wrote that stocks sold off because of President Trump's mixed messages, not because of tariff concerns. "We will not see a significant increase in tariffs on foreign imports to the U.S. and it is more likely that both China and Europe will reduce tariffs on U.S. goods as well," he said. "Reports from Beijing are already indicating that China is beginning to soften its Made in China 2025 program, which focuses on Chinese dominance in technology."
In case you forgot: As of today General Electric is no longer in the Dow. If it were still in, its more than 8% gain today would have made it the best performer in the index--even better than Apple (AAPL), today's top performer so far. Wall Street cheered after the company announced restructuring plans this morning . Walgreens, which replaced GE in the index today, is down more than 1% so far, and is the second-worst performer, beating only Intel (INTC).
"No one likes the new kid," wrote Ed Clissold , chief U.S. strategist at Ned Davis Research . He noted that Walgreens is the smallest (read wimpiest) in the Dow by market capitalization and takes the Dow farther away from its "industrial" origin. In fact, industrials are the biggest underweighted sector in the Dow relative to the S&P 500. The second-most underweight sector is consumer staples, where Walgreens sits categorically.
S&P 500: +0.4% to 2828.18
Dow 30: +89 points, or 0.4%, to 24,355.22
Nasdaq: +0.6% to 7571.24
Russell 2000: +0.3% 1514.17

10-year Treasury Yield: 2.88%
Midday Movers Akamai Technologies (AKAM) is down 3.1% to $75.17 after the company lowered its second-quarter earnings per share guidance, citing a stronger U.S. dollar.
Avis Budget is down 9.1% to $35.16 and Hertz Global is down 11.7% to $16.86 after Morgan Stanley resumed coverage of both stocks with an Underweight rating.
Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF) is up 1.1% to $8.49 after Macquarie initiated coverage with an Outperform rating.
Incyte Corp . (INCY) is down 6.4% to $67.15 after RBC Capital Markets downgraded it to Sector Perform.
Netflix (NFLX) is up 3.3% to $397.05, bouncing back from yesterday's losses, helped by Imperial Capital , which initiated coverage with a Buy rating. "We know of no single competitor that offers so much choice of content at this price point," writes analyst David Miller .
